follow-up time: 12 years (UK/New Zealand cohort) or 20 years (Swedish cohort)
exposure: Obstetric variables (collected before and during childbirth)
events around the time of childbirth

family history of each pelvic floor disorder

urinary incontinence before and during the index pregnancy

cohort: Pregnant women from the United Kingdom, New Zealand, and Sweden
finding: Prognostic models using obstetric variables were able to discriminate between women who did and did not experience pelvic floor disorders 12 or 20 years after delivery, with varying levels of accuracy depending on the specific disorder and predicted risk.
mod_finding: Route of delivery was a strong predictor in most models for developing pelvic floor disorders.
